patch.summary: Change a user's role or active state (admins; moderators may only suspend or reinstate members)
patch.description: Deactivating a user signs them out everywhere. A real suspension or reinstatement (is_active changing value) also emails the member at their stored address, after the change is saved; the email does not say who acted. Role changes and updates that change nothing send no email. Admins cannot demote or deactivate themselves. Moderators may send only is_active, and only for accounts whose role is user; they cannot change roles (sending the role a member already has is accepted and changes nothing) or touch admins, other moderators or themselves.

get.summary: List reviews to moderate (admins and moderators)
get.description: Reviews with text, plus removed ones (their text is gone). Each has status (flagged = unresolved reports, approved, pending, removed), reports_count, reasons, rating, sentiment and movie info. The page carries a summary with flagged and removed counts and the sentiment split; it covers the whole site, however the list is filtered.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search in review text, author name or username, applied before pagination.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Defaults to pending.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Only the reviews written by this member.

parameters.name: tmdb_id
parameters.description: Only the reviews of this title; add media_type to tell a movie from a TV show with the same id.

post.summary: Approve or reject several reviews at once (admins and moderators)
post.description: Applies one decision to up to 50 distinct reviews, each in its own transaction and exactly as PATCH /api/admin/reviews/{review} applies status: the same row locking, closing of open reports, audit entries and review_removed notices; the cached statistics are retired once at the end. One review failing never undoes the others. results lists every id in the order sent: status approved or rejected when the decision was applied, otherwise skipped with a reason: not_found (no such review), no_change (it already stood where the decision puts it and had no open reports) or failed (the decision could not be saved and was rolled back). applied counts the reviews the decision was applied to.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.summary: Get one review in full (admins and moderators)
get.description: Everything a queue row has (id, tmdb_id, media_type, rating, sentiment, has_spoilers, is_approved, moderation_labels, status, reports_count, reasons, movie, created_at), but with the whole text, plus removed_at, helpful_votes (how many members found it helpful; the app has no down-votes), an author block {id, name, username, role, is_active, reviews_with_text, removed_reviews, open_reports_against_their_reviews} and reports: every report filed against the review, open and closed, oldest first, each {id, status, reason, details, reporter {id, name, username}, resolved_by {id, name, username} or null, resolution_note, created_at, resolved_at}. The number of queries does not depend on the number of reports. Returned as {review}.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

patch.summary: Approve or reject a review, and set its spoiler flag (admins and moderators)
patch.description: Send status, has_spoilers or both; at least one is required. Rejecting removes the text, marks the review removed and keeps the member's star rating, and tells the author with a review_removed notification (the film only: never the text or who acted). Approving notifies nobody. Either decision closes the review's open reports. has_spoilers marks the review's text as containing spoilers or not; a change is recorded in the audit log as review.spoiler_changed (setting the value the review already has records nothing). With both, the two changes are applied in one transaction: if any part fails none of it is kept and nobody is notified. Setting has_spoilers to true on a review without text (a plain star rating or one whose text was removed, including by a rejection sent in the same request) is refused with 409 and nothing is changed; setting it to false on such a review changes nothing and is accepted, so rejected with has_spoilers false simply rejects. Returns {review}.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

409.description: has_spoilers true on a review that has no text.

422.description: Neither status nor has_spoilers sent, or a value is invalid.

delete.description: A review that still has text tells its author with a review_removed notification (the film only: never the text or who acted).

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.summary: List member reports to triage (admins and moderators)
get.description: Reports on reviews, room messages, movie lists, discussion rooms and member profiles, newest first. Open ones by default. Each has id, status (open, resolved, dismissed), reason, details, reporter {id, name, username}, target {type (review, message, list, room, profile), id, label, excerpt, owner {id, name, username} or null, removed}, resolved_by {id, name, username} or null, resolution_note, created_at and resolved_at. The excerpt is the message or review text cut to 200 characters, or a list title, room name or username. A report outlives its content: when the target was deleted (or a review's text was removed) the report stays and its target has removed true. For a deleted row the target shows the label and excerpt saved when the report was filed (a message is gone within a day) and no owner; a removed review shows no excerpt. The page carries a summary: by_status (counts of every report in each status) and by_target_type (counts of the reports still open on each kind of content).

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: Defaults to open; all lifts the filter.

parameters.name: reason
parameters.description: Review reasons are Spam, Links, Spoilers, Offensive language; the others are lowercase.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.description: The same shape as a row of the list, under `report`.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

patch.summary: Resolve or dismiss a report (admins and moderators)
patch.description: Triage only: the reported content is not touched, and the reporter is not told. With apply_to_target (default true) every other open report on the same content is closed with the same decision, note and staff member. Returns `report` and `reports_closed` (how many reports this decision closed, at least 1). Recorded in the audit log as report.resolved or report.dismissed (subject type report), with the status before and after, reports_closed and closed_report_ids (the ids closed, at most 100).

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.description: Each film has director, runtime, release_date, genre_ids and is_edited. The page carries summary.sync with cached, overrides and last_synced_at.

patch.summary: Hide, feature or edit a local movie
patch.description: Editing title, overview, director, runtime, release_date or genre_ids marks the film as edited only when a submitted value differs from the stored one; resending the same values changes nothing. null clears overview, director, runtime and release_date; an empty genre_ids clears the genres.

404.description: The film is not in the local catalogue.

get.summary: List TMDB genres with their local overrides (admins and moderators, read-only)
get.description: Every genre TMDB lists for the type, in TMDB's order, merged with its override: tmdb_id, tmdb_name, name (the one members see: name_override when set, else tmdb_name), name_override, is_hidden, position (null when not placed), movie_count and updated_at (null when there is no override). movie_count is the number of visible (not hidden) films in the local catalogue carrying the genre id; the catalogue holds films only, so it is always 0 for tv. Hidden genres are listed too. TMDB's list is cached for a day, the overrides are read on every request. Answers 502 when TMDB cannot be reached and its list is not cached.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Which genre list.

patch.summary: Rename, hide or place a genre (admins only)
patch.description: Sets the local override of the TMDB genre. Send any of name, is_hidden and position; what is not sent stays as it is, and null clears name or position. Values the genre already has change nothing and are not recorded; an override left with no name, no position and not hidden is removed. Returns the genre as the list shows it. Recorded in the audit log as genre.updated with the fields that changed. TMDB's cached list is not touched.

name.description: The name members see instead of TMDB's; null or empty clears it.

is_hidden.description: Leaves the genre out of the list offered to members.

position.description: Place in the list; genres with a position come first. Must be a JSON integer (not a boolean or a string).

delete.description: Removes the local override. Recorded in the audit log as genre.reset when there was one; resetting a genre without an override does nothing and records nothing. Works for an override whose genre TMDB no longer lists, and does not ask TMDB when there is no override.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

404.description: The type is neither movie nor tv.

get.summary: List every member's movie lists (admins and moderators)
get.description: Staff see all lists whatever their visibility and whatever their owner's profile visibility, and hidden films are counted: nothing is filtered out for them. Newest first, ties broken by id. Each row has id, title, description (cut to 200 characters), visibility (public or private: a list is either, followers-only is a profile setting), owner {id, name, username}, items_count, open_reports_count (open reports filed against the list), created_at and updated_at. The page carries a summary with the totals of all lists whatever the filters: total, public, private and reported (lists with an open report). The query count does not grow with the page.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Matches the list title, its owner's name or username (up to 100 characters).

parameters.name: reported
parameters.description: 1 for lists with an open report, 0 for lists without one.

get.description: The row of the list under `list`, with the description in full, its first 100 titles in position order as items {tmdb_id, media_type, title, poster_path, added_at} and the open reports against it as reports {id, reason, details, reporter {id, name, username}, created_at}, newest first. Titles and posters come from the local catalogue only (TMDB is never called), so a TV show or a film not in the catalogue has a null title and poster_path. Hidden films are listed.

patch.summary: Make a list private (admins and moderators)
patch.description: Staff can only restrict: visibility must be private, anything else is a 422. Making a public list private closes its open reports as resolved by the staff member, tells the owner with a list_restricted notification (action made_private, never who acted), and is recorded in the audit log as list.made_private (subject type list) with visibility from public to private and reports_resolved. A list that is private already is left alone: nothing is closed, recorded or sent. Returns the row under `list`.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

delete.description: Deletes the list and its titles through the MovieList module, closes its open reports as resolved by the admin, tells the owner with a list_restricted notification (action deleted) and records list.deleted in the audit log. Moderators get 403.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

delete.summary: Remove one title from a list (admins and moderators)
delete.description: Removes the movie (or, with type=tv, the TV show) with that TMDB id. 404 when the list does not hold it. Closes the list's open reports as resolved by the staff member, tells the owner with a list_restricted notification (action item_removed, with the film's tmdb_id and media_type) and records list.item_removed in the audit log with the removed tmdb_id and media_type and reports_resolved. Returns the row under `list`.

parameters.name: type
parameters.description: Defaults to movie.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.summary: List what staff did (admins only, read-only)
get.description: Newest first. Each entry has id, action, actor {id, name, username, role}, subject {type, id, label}, changes and created_at. The actor's role and the subject's label are the ones recorded at the time; actor id, name and username are null once that account is deleted, and the label keeps a deleted subject readable. changes maps each changed field to {from, to} (role, is_active, status of a review, movie fields, and for a genre its override name, is_hidden and position, where null means not set); an overview is only marked {changed: true}; a review decision also carries reports_resolved, the number of open reports it closed; a spoiler change (review.spoiler_changed) records has_spoilers {from, to}; it is null when there is nothing to compare (deletions). A movie's or genre's subject id is its tmdb_id; a genre's label is its TMDB name, with (TV) appended for a tv genre since movie and tv genres can share an id. A settings.updated entry (subject type setting) has a null subject id, the setting key as its label and one entry per setting that really changed: changes is {value: {from, to}} for a switch, and for the announcement each of enabled, level and expires_at that changed as {from, to} plus message: {changed: true} (the text is never logged). Resolving or dismissing a report (subject type report, label "Report on <type> #<id>") records its status from open to resolved or dismissed, reports_closed (the number of reports the decision closed) and closed_report_ids (their ids, at most 100). Deleting a star rating (subject type rating, label "Rating by <username> on <film title or id>") records {rating: {from: <stars>, to: null}, reports_deleted: <n>}, where reports_deleted is how many reports filed against the rating went with it (they have no foreign key); purging all of a member's ratings (action rating.purged, subject type user with the member's id, label "Ratings by <username>") records {removed: <count>, reports_deleted: <n>}. A list action (subject type list, label "List "<title>" by <username>") is list.made_private (changes visibility {from: public, to: private}), list.item_removed (tmdb_id and media_type of the removed title, each {from, to: null}) or list.deleted, each with reports_resolved, the number of open reports it closed. Only the changes that went through are recorded: an update that changes nothing records nothing, and neither does approving or rejecting a review whose status stays the same and that had no open reports, nor setting a review's spoiler flag to the value it has. Rows are never changed or removed.

parameters.name: actor_id
parameters.description: The staff member who acted.

parameters.name: subject_type
parameters.description: Required when subject_id is given.

parameters.name: subject_id
parameters.description: A user id, review id, movie tmdb_id, genre tmdb_id, report id, rating id or list id, depending on subject_type.

200.description: A page of audit log entries.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.description: Star-only ratings: reviews rows without text (reviews with text are never listed here; use /api/admin/reviews). Newest first, ties broken by id. Each row has id, tmdb_id, media_type, rating (1 to 5), moderated (true for the stars left behind when a moderator removed the review's text, i.e. removed_at is set; still listed and counted, but the rating tools never delete them), author {id, name, username}, film {tmdb_id, title, poster_path} (from the local catalogue only, never TMDB; null for a TV show or a film not stored) and created_at. The page carries a summary {total, average, distribution} over everything the filters match, not just the page: average is null without ratings (else rounded to two decimals) and distribution always has the keys "1" to "5".

parameters.name: tmdb_id
parameters.description: Only ratings of this title.

parameters.name: media_type
parameters.description: Only movies or only TV shows.

parameters.name: user_id
parameters.description: Only this member's ratings.

parameters.name: rating
parameters.description: Only this star value.

parameters.name: q
parameters.description: Case-insensitive search in the member's name or username; % and _ match literally.

200.description: A page of star ratings with its summary.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.summary: Get the star ratings of one film (admins and moderators)
get.description: total, average (null without ratings), distribution (keys "1" to "5") of the title's star-only ratings; with_text_count, the title's reviews with text (informational, not part of the other numbers); first_rated_at and last_rated_at (when its first and last star rating was left, null without any); and film {tmdb_id, title, poster_path} from the local catalogue (null when unknown or a TV show). A title nobody rated answers zeros, not 404.

parameters.name: media_type
parameters.description: Defaults to movie.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.summary: List members who left many star ratings in a short time (admins and moderators)
get.description: Rating-bombing detector. Counts each member's star-only ratings that were created inside the trailing window of `hours` hours ending now (changing the stars of an older rating does not move it into the window) and lists members with at least `min`, most ratings first and lowest member id first among equals. Each row is {user {id, name, username, created_at}, count, window_start, window_end}; the window is the same for every row. Reviews with text are not counted. A member has at most one rating per title, so count is also the number of titles rated.

parameters.name: hours
parameters.description: Window length in hours (default 1).

parameters.name: min
parameters.description: Fewest ratings in the window to be listed (default 20).

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

delete.summary: Delete one star rating (admins and moderators)
delete.description: Removes the rating and the reports filed against it. Any staff member may delete any one rating. A row that has review text, or that belongs to a moderated review (moderated true in the list), is not a plain rating: it is refused with 422 and must be removed through review moderation. Recorded in the audit log as rating.deleted (subject type rating, label "Rating by <username> on <film title or id>", changes {rating: {from: <stars>, to: null}, reports_deleted: <n>}) in the same transaction, and the cached dashboard statistics are refreshed. The member is not notified.

422.description: The row has review text or belongs to a moderated review; use review moderation.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

delete.summary: Delete every star rating of one member (admins and moderators)
delete.description: Rating-bombing clean-up: removes all of the member's star-only ratings (and the reports filed against them) in one transaction and answers {message, removed}. Their reviews with text and the rows of moderated reviews (moderated true) are untouched, with their reports; removed counts only the rows really deleted. A purge that removes nothing answers removed 0 and records nothing; otherwise it is recorded as rating.purged (subject type user, the member's id, label "Ratings by <username>", changes {removed: n, reports_deleted: <n>}). Admins may do this for anyone but themselves; moderators only for plain members (not admins, other moderators or themselves). The member is not notified.

403.description: Admins and moderators only, or the target is not allowed (own account, or a moderator acting on an admin or moderator).

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

get.description: Every setting, keyed by name, as {value, updated_at, updated_by}. A setting never changed has its default value and null updated_at and updated_by (updated_by is {id, name, username}, or null once that account is deleted). Keys: registration_open (default true), reviews_require_approval (false), review_auto_moderation (true), rooms_creation_enabled (true) and announcement {enabled, message, level, expires_at} (off by default).

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

patch.description: Send any subset of the settings; an unknown key, a wrong type or an empty body is a 422. registration_open=false refuses new password sign-ups and the first social sign-in of a new account with 403 code registration_closed (existing members still sign in). reviews_require_approval=true makes every new or edited review with text wait for a moderator. review_auto_moderation=false skips the AI moderation and publishes review text at once unless approval is required. rooms_creation_enabled=false refuses POST /api/rooms with 403 code rooms_creation_disabled (existing rooms keep working). The announcement is replaced as a whole: enabled and level are required, message is required while enabled (at most 300 characters after cleaning), expires_at is null or an ISO-8601 datetime with a timezone (UTC year 1970 to 2100; a month, day, hour 24, second 60 or offset past +/-14:00 is refused, a fraction of a second is dropped) that must be in the future only while the announcement is being enabled, so switching it off may keep or echo an old date. The message is plain text; clients must render it as text, never as HTML: control characters and text-direction marks are removed (line breaks are kept) and a message containing HTML tags is a 422. Only values that really differ are written, each recorded in the audit log in the same transaction; sending the current values changes and records nothing. Returns every setting as it is afterwards.

429.description: Too many requests (120 a minute per user).

value.description: A boolean, or the announcement object for the announcement key.

message.description: Plain text; render it as text, never as HTML.
Required while enabled. Plain text, no HTML tags; control characters are removed and line breaks kept. Clients must render it as text, never as HTML.

expires_at.description: ISO-8601 with a timezone, UTC year 1970 to 2100, offset at most +/-14:00. Stored as a UTC instant. Must be in the future only when enabled is true.
